items.summary: Security disposition is evidence_needed fleet-wide, blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, and conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Fleet-doctor has no run or results; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps have no results. Authentication boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are therefore unverified. TLS evidence shows no certificates expiring within 30 days only and does not establish complete TLS posture. Compliance is a technical baseline, not certification: 37 pass, 16 fail, and 6 unknown. Risk is high for public or security-sensitive release and medium for bounded changes that add no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Exact decision: retain private and preview-only gates, continue only read-only evidence capture, and permit ordinary reversible growth only within existing consent, disclosure, data-handling, claims, and rollback boundaries. Do not access credentials or private containers, exploit targets, alter permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue, or conduct outreach.

items.summary: Retain an evidence-needed fleet security disposition. Block public exposure and security-sensitive releases while material controls remain unevidenced; permit ordinary reversible growth only within existing boundaries and without new security or data risk.
items.requested_action: Continue the existing read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated, redacted evidence or explicit unknowns for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Keep private and preview-only launch gates where required. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue, or conduct external outreach.
